Lucky Cement Ltd Reports Steady Profit Growth Amid Robust Domestic Demand

KARACHI – Lucky Cement Ltd, one of Pakistan’s leading construction materials producers, posted steady growth in its quarterly financial results, buoyed by strong domestic demand and efficient cost management.

The company announced on Thursday that its net profit for the third quarter ended March 31 rose 8.2% year-on-year to PKR 3.25 billion, up from PKR 3.0 billion in the same period last year. Revenue increased by 10.5% to PKR 27.6 billion, reflecting both higher sales volumes and modest price improvements in local markets.

“Our focus on operational excellence and prudent financial management has helped us deliver another quarter of solid results,” said Ahmed Sohail, Chief Financial Officer at Lucky Cement Ltd. “Despite a competitive market environment, we have continued to optimize our production processes and strengthen our supply chain, resulting in improved margins.”

The company reported that local cement dispatches grew 12% year-on-year, while export volumes remained stable. Industry experts attribute the robust domestic sales to ongoing infrastructure development projects and increased construction activity in major urban centers.

“Cement demand has remained resilient, driven mainly by public sector infrastructure works and a pickup in private housing construction,” noted Asim Khurshid, an analyst at Crescent Securities. “Lucky Cement’s extensive distribution network has enabled it to capitalize on these trends, particularly in the northern and central regions.”

Cost of sales rose modestly, in line with higher fuel and energy prices, but Lucky Cement Ltd offset these pressures through efficiencies and a partial shift to alternative fuels at its Pezu and Karachi plants. The company also benefited from a favorable exchange rate, which helped stabilize input costs for imported raw materials.

The board of directors declared an interim cash dividend of PKR 2.50 per share, reflecting confidence in the company’s financial position and future outlook.

Industry insiders expect the momentum to continue over the coming months, with the All Pakistan Cement Manufacturers Association projecting a 6-8% growth in domestic cement consumption for the fiscal year. “If macroeconomic stability persists, the sector could see further upside,” said Zahra Malik, spokesperson for the association.

Lucky Cement Ltd closed trading on Thursday at PKR 570.25, up 1.3% on the day, outperforming the broader construction materials index.
